body.statement: From every subsequence of an array in \(\mathcal M\), one can extract a further subsequence such that, for the finitely many post knots, every scaled difference \(\sqrt{m_\ell}(c_{jtr,\ell}-c_{j'tr',\ell})\) converges in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\); the finite limits define within-cluster offsets \(d\), while absolute divergence defines distinct macro clusters. Along the same extraction, every \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\) converges in \([0,\infty]\) to \(h_j\), \(\rho_\ell\) converges in \([0,\infty]\), \(H_\ell\to H\), \(q_{t,\ell}\to q_t\) in \(L^2([0,1])^J\), \(M_{t,\ell}\to M_t\) for every post period, and the bounded jump and covariance coordinates admit joint limits. The maintained inequality for \(H_\ell\) passes to \(v^\top Hv\geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2\) on \(L\). This is a finite diagonal compactification, not a maintained local-alternative condition.
body.justification: The extraction turns all finite-or-diverging knot gaps and face distances into theorem-local coordinates and creates the limit Gram \(H\) from the maintained finite-array Grams \(H_\ell\), without narrowing the primitive model.
body.gap: Fang and Santos study fixed directionally differentiable maps; the compactification here is a finite diagonal argument specific to moving atomic knots and simplex faces, not an assumption borrowed from that paper.
body.consumer: It guarantees that every potentially nonconvergent sampling allocation has phase-law limit points that can be audited.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(K\leq (J+1)T_1(S-1)\) be the total number of retained post knots.  It is fixed by \(\mathrm{ass:fixed\mbox{-}panel}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:finite\mbox{-}post}\).  For each of the finitely many ordered pairs \((a,b)\) of knots, the sequence
\(\sqrt{m_\ell}(c_{a,\ell}-c_{b,\ell})\) takes values in the compact extended line \([-\infty,\infty]\).  Successive finite subsequence extractions therefore make all these differences converge simultaneously.  Declare \(a\sim b\) when the limit is finite.  Since exact differences add before taking a finite limit, this is an equivalence relation.  Its classes are the macro clusters.  Within a class choose one knot as origin; the limits relative to that origin are the offsets \(d\).  Between different classes the absolute scaled difference diverges.

Each \(\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}\) lies in \([0,\infty]\), and \(\rho_\ell\) lies in the same compactified half-line.  A further finite diagonal extraction gives all limits \(h_j\) and the limit of \(\rho_\ell\).  Because \(\sum_j\sqrt{n_\ell}w_{\ell j}=\sqrt{n_\ell}\to\infty\) by \(\mathrm{ass:sample\mbox{-}divergence}\), at least one coordinate of \(h\) is infinite.

All quantile functions take values in the common compact outcome interval of length \(D\).  Translate that fixed interval once, which does not change differences or any quadratic restricted to \(L\), and regard the functions as bounded in \([0,D]\).  A bounded sequence of monotone functions has a pointwise-convergent subsequence at every continuity point of a monotone limit: this follows by diagonal extraction on the rationals followed by monotonicity.  The discontinuity set is countable, so dominated convergence gives \(L^2\) convergence.  Applying this argument to the finitely many donor--period sequences produces \(q_{t,\ell}\to q_t\) in \(L^2([0,1])^J\).  Therefore, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \|M_{t,\ell}-M_t\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \|q_{t,\ell}-q_t\|_2
       (\|q_{t,\ell}\|_2+\|q_t\|_2)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The same boundedness makes the entries of \(H_\ell\) lie in a fixed compact interval, so another finite extraction gives \(H_\ell\to H\).  Atom locations, masses, jumps, and the finitely many multinomial covariance entries are bounded; hence they too have joint convergent subsubsequences.  These extractions can be nested because their number is finite.

For any \(v\in L\), \(\mathrm{ass:strong\mbox{-}gram}\) and entrywise convergence give
\[
 v^\top Hv=\lim_\ell v^\top H_\ell v
 \geq\lambda\|v\|_2^2.
\]
No local convergence condition has been imposed on the original array: the coordinates were obtained only after selecting a limit point from each compactified finite-dimensional sequence.
